newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares extend gains, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares extend gains, seen stabilising.

text.p: Polish shares on Wednesday rose for the fifth session running, despite some expectations of falls, and analysts said another gain seemed likely on Thursday after strong buying after price-fixing and at continuous trade.
But analysts said the market was rebounding from last week's steep falls and that overall prices were not low enough to spark a significant growth trend amid a lack of signals.

"I think we're having rather a technical rebound rather than a fundamental one -- prices of some stocks fell...and speculative investors are taking positions," said Cezary Markiewicz, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.7 percent to 16,362.2 points and turnover rose 6.9 percent to 194.9 million zlotys ($62.7 million) on all three markets. Gainers led losers by 40 to 35 with 18 stocks flat.

Analysts said the start of a heavy primary market season, starting with next week's public offering of paper firm Celuloza Swiecie SA of at least 112.5 million zlotys ($36.2 million), could keep some investors away from listed stocks.
They said the threat that more signficant falls could ensue on major Western bourses and spread to Warsaw was also dampening some demand.

Analysts said cable maker Kable surged 10 percent to 45.1 zlotys ($14.5) after Danish-based 50-percent owner NKT Cables on Monday called a public tender offer to buy Kable's remaining one million shares at the then market price of 41 zlotys ($13.2).
The stock did not trade after price-fixing due to excess demand, which traders said signalled another rise on Thursday.
Biggest loser Espebepe plunged 9.8 percent after a recent surge as players continued to speculate on whether the builder with 75 million zlotys ($24.1) in debts would survive.
